preamble: Raising and centralization of the close-mid back rounded vowel [o] to the near-close near-back [ʊ]. In Northern Standard Dutch and in the Randstad, the long close-mid vowels /eː, øː, oː/ are otherwise realized with closing glides (over /oːvər/ [ouvər]). Before /r/ in the same word they lose the glide and are raised and slightly centralized to [ɪː, ʏː, ʊː], often with a schwa-like off-glide ([ɪə, ʏə, ʊə]). Syllable-final /oː/ in compounds is not affected: bureauredactrice [byˈroʊredɑkˌtrisə] 'desk editor (f.)'. Belgian Standard Dutch keeps [oː] in the same words (noordenwind [ˈnoːrdə(n)wɪnt]).

languageExamples.context: Before /r/ in the same word, except syllable-final /oː/ in compounds

examples.note: Both forms are from the Northern Standard Dutch sample text (Gussenhoven 1999) on Wikipedia, which in the same passage has over /oːvər/ as [ouvər].
Also realized as a centering diphthong [ʊə], especially before coda /r/.
